thread:
infra-sre: paging: p99 spike detected for streaming requests routed through LB cluster us-east-1a -> observed streaming stalls and long tail (p95 ~ 450ms -> p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.8s). alert: /metrics/router/latency >= threshold.

incident-bot: Alert created: INC-2029-8743. Page sent to @sam_oncall and @elaine_prodops.

sam_oncall: got the page, joining. any obvious deploys or config changes?

mike_rt: no deploys in last 30m. I see a sudden rise in 503+retry from clients behind the LB (connection retries). Top source IPs concentrated to a handful of pods behind router-3.

luis_net: net telemetry shows uneven distribution across zones; us-east-1a has ~65% of traffic for this pool, other zones <20%. load balancer weights look skewed for the pool id "inference-prod-pool-7".

elaine_prodops: customer-impact: several mid-market customers report degraded streaming responsiveness; CS triage says 3 customers complaining about repeated stalls. flagged as potential SLO breach for hosted-api (p99 target 2s).

sam_oncall: OK plan: 1) isolate hot partition (identify hot keys/clients) 2) temporarily adjust LB weights away from us-east-1a 3) fallback to model-variant with smaller KV footprint for affected requests if remap fails. who can adjust LB weights now?

luis_net: I can bump weights. doing a quick dry-run:
```
# dry-run: show weights for pool
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/pools/inference-prod-pool-7 | jq '.zones'
```

luis_net: current weights: us-east-1a=0.65, us-east-1b=0.18, us-east-1c=0.17. I'm going to reduce us-east-1a to 0.3 and redistribute. Applying now.

mike_rt: applying an eager fallback for streaming: patching router policy to allow smaller batch size for requests with seq_len>512 so they use low-latency path. patch: 
```
PATCH /router/policies/streaming
{
  "match": "seq_len>512",
  "action": {"variant":"low_kv","batch_max_tokens":64}
}
```

incident-bot: config change recorded: /router/policies/streaming patched by mike_rt.

infra-sre: monitoring: p95 dropped from 1.1s -> 720ms within 90s of weight change. p99 now ~1.6s and trending down. but still seeing intermittent streaming stalls attributed to a small set of client keys.

sam_oncall: can we identify hot keys? run a top-k on prefix cache misses and long tail traces.

mike_rt: pulled traces for top 200 slow requests, 72% share a single client-id header: client_x-87. Looks like a bursty traffic pattern from that client causing KV cache hotness + router queueing.

elaine_prodops: contacting CS: notify affected customers with ETA ~30 mins for full mitigation. Prepare a short blurb.

eng-runtime: note: model-variant low_kv increased CPU per token slightly but significantly lowered average token latency for long sequences. good trade for now.

sam_oncall: temporary mitigation checklist: 1) weight redistribution (done) 2) apply router policy fallback (done) 3) limit concurrent streams per client to 10 for pool (enqueue extras) 4) patch LB to enforce per-client token-rate cap of 5k/min if feasible. can someone apply (3)?

luis_net: pushing rate-limit rule to LB config (rate-limit by header client-id):
```
PUT /lb/config/pools/inference-prod-pool-7/rate-limits
{"client_limit": 5000, "concurrent_streams": 10}
```
Applying now.

incident-bot: LB rate-limit change queued; will roll out gradually.

infra-sre: after rate-limit and fallback, p99 stabilized ~1.2s, p95 ~380ms. streaming stall errors dropped 92%. customer complaints reduced to 1 ongoing.

sam_oncall: good. need a short incident record for on-call handoff. summarizing:
- root cause hypothesis: LB weight skew + one hot client causing router queueing and KV cache hot partition -> tail amplification.
- mitigations: redistributed LB weights, enabled low_kv variant for long seqs, applied per-client concurrent stream cap + rate-limit.
- customer impact: transient SLO breach at p99 for ~18 minutes; 3 customers reported interruptions, 1 still under monitoring but improving.
- follow-ups: deep dive on why weight skew occurred (autoscaler / weight calc bug), consider stricter imbalance alarms, implement hotkey re-routing rule in router, add rate-limit telemetry per client.

elaine_prodops: creating follow-up ticket: INC-FOLLOWUP-2029-8743, assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre. will coordinate postmortem.

mike_rt: adding runbook update: when p99 spike + hotkey detected -> immediate fallback to low_kv + temp rate-limit.

sam_oncall: handing off to oncall rotation backup @elaine_prodops for monitoring during the next hour. I'm off-call in 20. please escalate if p99 > 2s again.

elaine_prodops: acknowledged. monitoring dashboards pinned. I'll keep CS updated.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2029-8743 updated: status=mitigated, services=router,lb,inference. timeline attached in tracker.

sam_oncall: thanks team. we'll run a blameless postmortem tomorrow.

mike_rt: saving logs/trace bundle to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2029-8743/trace-bundle.tar.gz

infra-sre: closing thread here after handoff.
